description.value:
Primary Attribute: Presence

Every manifestation is an agreement with something. Most casters don't read what they signed. You did, you do, and you keep what you signed for.

Manifestation Discipline: Upkeep / concurrency specialist (5-pt budget — Upkeep ●●●, Misfire ●●, Clarity ●, Reach ●, Signature Mode: Sealed Pact)

Class Identity

Tier cap and footprint stay universal. What you have is holding: more concurrent manifestations sustained at once, lower upkeep on bargained subjects, and the right to renegotiate a misfire instead of eating it. Pactkeepers don't manifest bigger — they manifest more, longer, and in writing.

Class Features

  • Initiation 1 — The Bargain. The Pact slot comes online (existing class resource — see your Doctrine for the generation / tier rule). While a creature, object, or place is bargained-with as your Pact subject, you may sustain one additional manifestation on or near them at no extra upkeep against your Clarity. Skill rank +1 in two of: Diplomacy, Insight, Intimidation, Lore.
  • Initiation 6 — Renegotiate. When one of your manifestations would misfire, you may instead accept a GM-set narrative debt (a future scene, a future cost, a future favor owed) and treat the manifestation as having succeeded at base tier. The debt is real; the GM's table runs the bill.
  • Initiation 11 — Sealed Pact (Signature Mode). Stance. While the Seal holds, your concurrent-manifestation cap is +2, and you cannot voluntarily drop a manifestation sustained on a pact-bound subject (the seal carries the upkeep, not your moment-to-moment will). Pays ongoing upkeep against your Clarity. (Pilot: lock exact upkeep curve and break condition after one playtest cycle.)
  • Initiation 16 — Ledger Day. 1/Soma Break, transfer one of your sustained manifestations to a willing ally — they pick up upkeep from their Clarity from that point on. The pact moves with the paper, not the person who originally signed.

Doctrines

See your Doctrine document for the L1 Pact slot generation rule and the rest of the doctrine ladder. Doctrines remain the depth lane — the Discipline budget above is what you bring to any Pact-shape.

Carryover Notes

  • Existing Pact / pool mechanics are preserved; concurrency-bonus above stacks with pool spend, not a replacement.
  • Tier cap, footprint, Clarity max are universal. Holding power is the only knob you bend.
Administrative Pressure measures the bureaucratic and metaphysical strain you generate by making reality hold still.
Civic Charge is permission, credibility, and stabilizing authority made spendable. This is your display item for current Civic Charge and Administrative Pressure on the Features tab.

“This happened. It matters. Act accordingly.”

When a significant action succeeds or fails, you may establish a Precedent tied to a creature, location, faction, or concept. While active, similar future actions reroll the lowest die if aligned with the precedent, or suffer disadvantage if they violate it. You are not forcing outcomes—you are making contradiction expensive.

Precedent is probability gravity, not mind control.

“Reality is consistent because someone keeps the minutes.”

Administrative Pressure: +3

You are licensed to administer continuity of meaning: what counts as having happened, how strongly the past pulls on the present, and which version of events becomes official.

Esoteric Bias: Divination (Chokhmah) and Illusion (Hod). When casting manifestations from these schools, misalignment penalties are suppressed; aligned casting generates +1 Civic Charge.

Always Prepared Manifestations: Detect Thoughts, Zone of Truth, Clairvoyance, Modify Memory, Legend Lore.

Unique Contract: Binding Precedent (see Pactkeeper features).

🧭 PACTKEEPER FEATURE: Jurisdiction

Type: Permanent class feature (Level 1)
Purpose: Defines what you are authorized to administer

A Jurisdiction does not grant power directly.
It grants permission.

What Jurisdiction Does

Your Jurisdiction determines:

  • Which situations generate Civic Charge more easily

  • Which effects you may enforce without Pressure

  • Which Contracts you can issue by default

  • Which manifestations are considered “in mandate”

Example:

  • A Steward acting on community morale = in mandate

  • A Steward issuing divine sanctions = out of mandate (Pressure risk)

Jurisdiction Is NOT:

  • A resource pool

  • A bonus to rolls

  • A manifestation list restriction

It is a scope limiter and Pressure filter.

“Godhood is community service. I’m here to keep the lights on.”

Manifesting (Delegated): You are a full prepared caster. Your manifesting is routed through stabilized civic thoughtforms (tulpas), retired gods, and the Long Quiet—reducing volatility and preventing raw backlash.

Civic Charge: You maintain a pool of Civic Charge used to cite precedent, stabilize outcomes, and enforce contracts. Your subclass and Jurisdiction determine how you gain and spend it.

Delegated Channeling: When you cast a manifestation, you treat esoteric misalignment as neutral (no penalty). When you cast in alignment with your Jurisdiction, you convert alignment into resources rather than raw power.

🟣 PACTKEEPER — CORE MECHANICS

🗂 CLASS RESOURCE: Civic Charge

Type: Dice-based resource pool
Purpose: Represents institutional authority, social mandate, and metaphysical clearance

Civic Charge Dice

  • Start as d6

  • Increase at:

    • Level 5 → d8

    • Level 11 → d10

    • Level 17 → d12

  • Maximum stored dice:
    = your Soul modifier (minimum 1)

You cannot store Civic Charge beyond this limit.

Gaining Civic Charge

You gain 1 Civic Charge Die when any one of the following occurs:

  • You successfully stabilize a volatile situation
    (panic, corruption, escalation, social collapse)

  • You resolve a conflict without increasing Violence

  • You enforce a binding Contract or Precedent

  • You complete a meaningful ritual, mediation, or closure action

  • You cast a manifestation in esoteric alignment (correct correspondence / timing)

Limit:
You may gain only 1 Civic Charge Die per round.

Spending Civic Charge

When you spend a Civic Charge Die, roll it and apply the result as one of the following:

  • Stabilization: Reduce incoming damage, panic, corruption, or fallout by the rolled amount

  • Authority Boost: Add the rolled value to a manifestation DC, contested roll, or enforcement check

  • Enforcement: Force a reroll against a Contract or Precedent (target takes the worse result)

  • Containment: Convert a catastrophic outcome into a controlled one

  • Closure: End an ongoing effect cleanly instead of explosively

Each use consumes the die.

Running Out of Civic Charge

If you have 0 Civic Charge Dice:

  • You may still cast manifestations and use features

  • But you cannot:

    • Enforce contracts

    • Prevent escalation

    • Convert failures into clean outcomes

You are now acting without mandate, which invites pushback.

⚖ PUSHBACK SYSTEM: Administrative Pressure

Pactkeepers do not suffer backlash.
They accumulate Administrative Pressure.

You gain Pressure when:

  • You act outside your Jurisdiction

  • You override community consent

  • You force outcomes repeatedly

  • You ignore due process or precedent

Effects of Pressure (GM-facing bands)

  • Low: NPCs question authority, cooperation drops

  • Moderate: Enforcement costs increase, resistance grows

  • High: Mandates contested, Auditors intervene, Jurisdiction narrows

Pressure Points

Administrative Pressure is tracked as points, not just bands.

  • Low: 1–2 Pressure
  • Moderate: 3–5 Pressure
  • High: 6+ Pressure

Pressure is still narrative, but these thresholds provide a visible meter for play.

Clearing Pressure

  • Downtime

  • Proper closure

  • Delegation to other systems

  • Subclass features (Steward, Decommissioner especially)

Pressure is narrative, but persistent.

“I’m citing case law.”

Administrative Pressure: −2

Spend Civic Charge to invoke the record:

  • Cite Precedent: Force a reroll by asserting consistency. If the action violates an established precedent, the reroll takes the worse result.
  • Establish Record: Lock an outcome as official for purposes of consequence and precedent.
  • Suppress Contradiction: Nullify paradox, contradictory magic, or narrative retcons for one moment.
  • 📑

📑 PACTKEEPER FEATURE: Precedent

Type: Persistent world state marker
Purpose: Makes outcomes stick and repetition matter

Precedents are not dice. They are flags on reality.

Creating a Precedent

A Precedent is created when:

  • A major action succeeds or fails

  • A Contract is enforced

  • A significant moral or political line is crossed

  • A Pactkeeper explicitly declares one (Archivist specialty)

What a Precedent Does

While active, a Precedent causes:

  • Repeated similar actions to:

    • Suffer disadvantage, or

    • Trigger automatic consequences

  • NPCs and systems to “expect” consistency

  • Reality to resist contradiction

Interacting with Precedent

Pactkeepers may spend Civic Charge to:

  • Cite a Precedent (force rerolls)

  • Lock an outcome as official

  • Suppress contradictory magic or retcons

Archivists gain expanded control over this.

Ending a Precedent

A Precedent ends when:

  • It is superseded

  • It is resolved narratively

  • It is formally revoked

  • A Decommissioner retires it

Crew Type (Bad Eden): Cultural Ambassadors.

“A smile is a blade if you know where to put it.”

Cultural Ambassadors weaponize hospitality. They learn your customs, flatter your saints, and find the one story you tell yourself to stay brave. Then they use it to open doors—or to make you open them.

  • Tactical Identity: You gain a skill rank in Performance and Diplomacy.
  • Strategic Identity: Your faction starts with +1 Soft Power OPs.

Judgment - Necessary force. +1 Violence, +1 Logistics OPs

Geburah draws the line. It rewards discipline, enforcement, and decisive action against fortified problems, but always risks becoming cruelty if severity outruns wisdom.

Occult Association (Bad Eden): Goetic Summoner.

“I have friends. They’re just… contractual.”

Goetic Summoners do not worship. They do not submit. They negotiate.

To a Goetic, the Great Work is not merely a path of purification. It is a war over leverage. Power exists in the Shatterlands, and much of it has teeth, names, appetites, and terms. If you can name it, you can sometimes bind it. If you can bind it, you can make it useful. For a while.

Goetics build circles, memorize taboos, track debts, and turn predatory forces into temporary infrastructure. They call this control. The world calls it an incident report waiting to happen.

How Goetics pursue the Great Work:

  • By extracting leverage from Qliphothic forces instead of merely resisting them
  • By binding hazards into assets and paying the price later
  • By treating Darkness as a resource with teeth
  • By weaponizing fear, coercion, and forbidden access where cleaner traditions would hesitate

Resonance: Qliphoth / Shadow — rupture, appetite, inversion, and the dangerous intelligence inside corruption.

Tell-tales: counted names, precise circles, a room that feels like it already agreed to terms before anyone spoke.

Faction Effects (Passive):

  • +1 to Violence OP rolls
  • +1 to Intrigue OP rolls

Cost Principle: every Goetic gain creates obligation. Expect Debt, escalating Darkness pressure, hostile notice, and consequences that remember your name longer than you wanted them to.

“Everything has a price. You just admit it.”

Archetype (Bad Eden): The Devil (Exploiter). You are leverage without innocence. Debt, temptation, extraction, and the cold mathematics of turning weakness into yield.

Archetype Effects

  • Faction Edge. Your archetype strengthens predatory bargaining, economic pressure, and profit under corruption. This Archetype is associated with +1 Economy in faction calculus.
  • Tier Engine. See this Archetype’s Tier feats (Tier 1–4) for your full tactical and strategic toolkit.

Locks are promises made by people who never met you.

Rules

You reroll the lowest die on checks made to locate hidden doors, panels, caches, and secret compartments.

Additionally, when you attempt to open a lock or disable a trap, you may treat a 2d10x10 roll of 9 or lower as a 10. Once you use this principle, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or Sanctuary.

Calm the Mob

Crowds don’t think. They feel. So you give them something else to feel.

Rules

You gain a skill rank in Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence) (your choice). If you already have it, you gain mastery.

When you spend at least 1 minute addressing a group of non-hostile or uncertain creatures, you may make a Presence (Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence)) check (DC set by the GM). On a success, you reduce immediate hostility: the crowd hesitates, disperses, or agrees to hear terms. On a failure, you still buy time, but a complication occurs (a challenger steps forward, guards arrive, a rumor spreads).

Initiation 6 — Renegotiate. When one of your manifestations would misfire, you may instead accept a GM-set narrative debt (a future scene, a future cost, a future favor owed) and treat the manifestation as having succeeded at base tier. The debt is real; the GM's table runs the bill.

Out here, healing is logistics.

You gain a skill rank in Faith (Soul). If you already have it, you gain mastery.

When you use a medkit to stabilize a creature, it also regains Integrity equal to your skill rank bonus.

Additionally, during a Respite, you may allow up to two creatures to regain additional Integrity equal to your skill rank bonus. A creature can benefit from this principle only once per Respite.

Grim Persistence

You are difficult to kill because you do not stop.

Rules

Your Integrity maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your level. Additionally, once per Sanctuary, when you are reduced to 0 Integrity but not killed outright, you may remain at 1 Integrity instead.

Improvised Engineer

If you can’t fix it, you can at least make it dangerous.

Rules

You gain skill rank with artisan’s tools of your choice. If you already have it, you gain mastery.

During a Respite, you can craft one improvised device from scrap (choose one):

  • Flash-burn: A thrown device (20/60) that sheds bright light in a 2 squares radius for 1 minute; creatures that rely on invisibility have their invisibility suppressed while in the light (GM adjudication).
  • Snareline: A 2 squares tripline trap you can set in 1 minute; the first creature to cross it must succeed on a Intrigue check (DC = 8 + your skill rank bonus + your Mind value) or fall prone.
  • Signal Screamer: A noisemaker you can place; it triggers on contact, audible out to 60 squares

A device becomes inert after 8 hours or after triggering once.

Click this feature on the sheet to mark spent and post the chat card. Reset on Soma Break.

Scavenged Insight (Soul)

Debris tells stories.

Rules

After a combat encounter, you may ask the GM one factual question about what the enemies were carrying, guarding, or afraid of.

Situational Mastery

Every fight begins with a choice.

Rules

At the start of each combat, choose one: reroll the lowest die on your first attack roll, reroll the lowest die on your first defense checks, or +2 squares movement until the end of your first turn.

manifestation.thirdThing: Anyone who lies inside the field is marked: they cough at the moment of the lie. Other people in the field hear it and know.

system.flavor: She set the ledger on the table. She did not need to open it. He withdrew the offer.

manifestation.concept: A ledger — physical or implied — that records every promise spoken near you. The book updates itself. It is impossible to write in falsely.
manifestation.durationText: Persistent. The ledger is a campaign-relevant artifact.
manifestation.riskText: Other Pactkeepers, archivists, and major faction lawyers will want to read it. Some will pay. Some will threaten.
manifestation.pathResonance: Pactkeeper (Archivist) — the long memory of the office.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You have a book that nobody can lie to. Including you.
manifestation.gmCalibration: Tier-3 Form. Strategic-tier item. Excellent for long-arc political play.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: Once per session, consult the ledger about a recent promise made in your presence. The ledger names the promise verbatim, the promiser, and any clauses.
manifestation.signature: Pages turn at quiet moments without being touched. Ink gathers on the page like dew.
manifestation.thirdThing: Over a season, the ledger accumulates enough material to embarrass any institution that has lied to you.

system.damageFlavor: the consequence of an oath broken
system.flavor: She had heard him swear. When he lied, the lie cut him.

manifestation.concept: When an oath sworn in your presence is broken, the breaker takes the wound the oath promised them.
manifestation.durationText: Resolves at the moment of breaking.
manifestation.riskText: Reality charges interest. If the oath was vague, the penalty may be misapplied. If it was specific, the penalty is exact.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You can make an oath bite back when it is broken. Witnessed oaths are not free.
manifestation.gmCalibration: T1 Working. Requires you to have witnessed the oath. Conditional but devastating when triggered.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: Reaction: when a creature within Near range breaks an oath sworn in your witness, deal 2d6 psychic damage and apply a condition appropriate to the broken oath.
manifestation.signature: A faint snap of a sealed scroll. The breaker visibly winces.
manifestation.thirdThing: The wound is the wound the breaker themselves named when they swore. Reality pays out exactly what was promised.

system.flavor: He buttoned the robe. He had not lied since the year he forged it.

manifestation.concept: A worn vestment — robe, sash, ring — into which you have hammered an oath you keep to yourself. While you wear it, your word carries weight.
manifestation.durationText: Bound to you while you keep the oath.
manifestation.riskText: Breaking the oath costs 1 Blood Debt and the vestment is ruined. Other Pactkeepers will know.
manifestation.pathResonance: Pactkeeper (Steward) — the sworn life made tactile.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You are recognized as a person whose word counts. Until you break it.
manifestation.gmCalibration: Tier-1 Form. The oath must be specific and named at forging. GM enforces.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: +2 to social rolls when you give your word. Once per scene, when you make a promise, all parties present recognize it as binding without requiring further ceremony.
manifestation.signature: The garment is plain but absolutely clean — it does not stain, fray, or weather.
manifestation.thirdThing: If you break the oath, the garment changes — visibly. The change is recognized by every Pactkeeper.

Resonant. On a clean hit, the target's next manifestation has +1 misfire bias.

description.value:
A reinforced heater shield carried by Pactkeeper enforcers, its rim engraved with a standing oath the bearer renews each dawn. When the oath holds, so does the shield — vow-resin lacing snags incoming force and feeds it into the bearer's stance.

Eat the Blow (1/Soma Break). While attuned and equipped, the bearer may shift one die of incoming kinetic damage into Stress instead of Integrity. GM-adjudicated; tap the use tracker when spent. Resists kinetic passively.
